No, that is not true.

Under the Swiss political system, a popular initiative that is accepted by a majority of the voters in a national vote becomes binding. Once the people have approved an initiative through a referendum, the Swiss Federal Council (the executive branch) and the Federal Assembly (which includes the National Council and the Council of States, i.e., the parliament) do not have the authority to reject it. The initiative must be implemented as per the will of the people.

The Federal Council is obligated to put the initiative into effect through appropriate legislative or administrative measures. The parliament may debate and refine the implementation process, but it cannot block the implementation of a popular initiative that has been approved by the electorate.
